general_information.Description: Main objective: This course is designed to develop advanced knowledge, managerial thinking, and professional competencies essential for executive housekeepers in hotel and lodging establishments. Students will acquire expertise in departmental organization, asset and inventory management, human resources, quality assurance, risk and environmental management, and the integration of professional ethics and sustainable practices to enhance both operational efficiency and guest satisfaction. -Description: Through a comprehensive structure reflecting current industry standards, the course explores the strategic and technical responsibilities of executive housekeepers, including department planning; organizing, directing, and controlling resources; budget and labor control; equipment, laundry, and cleaning operations; as well as health, safety, and environmental leadership. Emphasis is placed on human resource management, communication and teamwork in multicultural environments, problem-solving, total quality management (TQM), and effective interaction with other hotel divisions to achieve organizational goals. Case studies, practical issues (from the textbook), and real-world scenarios are incorporated to strengthen the link between theory and practice, while fostering ethics and adaptability in decision-making. -Teaching method: A blend of teaching strategies is adopted, including interactive lectures, case study analysis, group discussion, skill demonstration, management simulation, situational problem-solving, collaborative projects, and hands-on practice drawn from the textbook’s minicases and operational cases. Students are assessed through a variety of methods—applied exercises, quizzes, group/individual assignments, scenario analyses, and projects—focusing on both knowledge integration and the application of managerial and technical skills to real and simulated housekeeping challenges. -Completion Criteria: Every on-going assessment component > 0; Final Result >=5 & Final Exam Score >= 4
general_information.StudentTasks: Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Comply with the time and regulation - Professional grooming - Respect and protect school asset. - Strongly communication and teamworking.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Analyze the role, organization, and professional standards of the housekeeping department within different types of lodging establishments; explain how housekeeping interacts with other divisions to optimize guest experience.

Evaluate and apply advanced management concepts relevant to executive housekeeping, including planning, organizing, directing, coordinating, and controlling resources to achieve departmental and organizational goals.
Effectively implement inventory management, cost control, and budgetary practices in housekeeping operations, ensuring efficient utilization of equipment, supplies, and labor.
Demonstrate knowledge and skills in managing technical operations: cleaning procedures, laundry, floor care, and preventive maintenance in compliance with quality standards and safety regulations.
Manage human resources in the housekeeping department: from recruiting, training, motivating, evaluating, to fostering an inclusive and productive work environment.
Analyze and respond to emerging risks related to safety, security, infectious diseases, and implement sustainable environmental management practices in lodging properties.
Develop effective communication, team leadership, and problem-solving skills to address operational challenges, guest complaints, and multicultural workforce dynamics in the housekeeping department.

Demonstrate professional ethics, responsibility, and adaptability in decision-making as an executive housekeeper; contribute to the sustainable development and competitive advantage of the hospitality organization.

assessments.Question Type: Option 1: Four or five students per group and Each group selects a hypothetical medium-sized hotel and develops a “housekeeping management proposal.” The proposal consists of three main parts: (1) designing the organizational structure and briefly describing the functions of positions within the housekeeping department, together with the basic coordination flow with other hotel departments; (2) creating a staffing plan and work schedule for the housekeeping department based on an assumed number of rooms and occupancy level, explaining the principles of efficient labor utilization; and (3) choosing one of two directions – either developing a housekeeping service quality management policy (room inspection checklist, guest complaint-handling procedure) or developing a policy for staff development and retention in the housekeeping department (training, motivation, evaluation).. Option 2 (For Constructivism Approach only): Follow lecturer's proposal.
